title: Negotiation mental map and clause hypotheses
content:
Purpose: quick mental model for talking through contract redlines with engineering/SEs during pre-sales and with Sales during closes. This is a working map — short phrases, hypotheses to test, and quick scripts I can read aloud. Not polished; use as in-meeting cue sheet.

High-level goals (prioritized):
- Protect data residency & export controls without blocking Dedicated/Private deals.
- Limit long-tail liability exposure (indemnity + consequential damage) while keeping recourse simple.
- Make transition/exit clean (handover of data, key rotations, escrows when necessary).
- Keep commercial friction low: prefer operational controls > monetary concessions.

Quick mental anchors (how to triage clause severity on first pass):
1) Customer data sensitivity (P0): PHI/PII/Financial — escalate to Security & Compliance immediately.
2) Operational counterparty risk (P1): Subprocessor lists, right to audit — can usually solve with narrow SLAs and SOC reports.
3) Liability redlines (P2): caps, indemnity pigs — negotiate band, tie to fees, avoid unlimited exposure.
4) IP/output language (P2): model output IP claims — prefer license to customer for their inputs/outputs; resist broad ownership grabs.
5) Termination/transition (P2): ensure data return + deletion window + support for export.
6) Export/residency/escrow (P3): important for regulated verticals, but often sales can accept add-on.

Clauses to watch — immediate flags and suggested counter-language (shorthand):
- Unlimited liability / no cap
  Flag: red. Ask for cap tied to 12 months of paid fees; carve out for gross negligence/fraud. Script: "We can accept meaningful remedies for gross negligence but need a predictable commercial cap — 12 months of fees preserves recovery without open-ended risk."

- Broad indemnity (IP + third-party claims + customer outputs)
  Flag: red/orange depending on scope. Push for narrowed indemnity to claims arising from our actual code/violations, not downstream outputs. Script: "We indemnify claims arising from our services and code; for customer output/IP disputes, propose mutual indemnity or reliance on termination rights instead."

- Data usage / model training rights
  Flag: orange. Customer asks to prevent us from using their data to train public models. Our play: offer opt-out for Dedicated/Private; hosted: offer contractual promise not to train on identified customer datasets plus technical isolation where reasonable. Script: "We treat customer data as not used for model training by default for enterprise tiers; for hosted, we can provide contractual assurances and data segregation options."

- Broad audit & access rights (unbounded right to audit infrastructure)
  Flag: orange. Prefer SOC2 reports + scoped audits with notice and confidentiality. Script: "We provide SOC2 and accommodate on-site audits under NDA and with scope/time limits; open-ended remote access to infra is a non-starter."

- Term + automatic renewal + long notice windows
  Flag: yellow. Push for reasonable auto-renewal (30–60 days) and shorter notice for non-renewal for more flexibility.

- Data return & deletion timelines ambiguous
  Flag: yellow. Ask for explicit 30–90 day window and certified deletion, include list of retained logs and retention windows. Script: "We will return customer data on request and certify deletion within 45 days; logs for security/ops retained for up to 90 days unless otherwise agreed."

- Export/data residency restrictions that block routing/fallbacks
  Flag: red/orange. If customer forbids cross-region fallback, note operational risk. Counter: carve-out for emergency cross-region failover with notification and encryption in transit + at rest.

Negotiation levers (what they can concede):
- Increase fees for stricter residency or dedicated hardware.
- Agreed SOC2/SOC3 attestation cadence and shared audit artifacts.
- Escrow / escrow-lite for select cryptographic keys (cost to customer).
- Shorter SLA credits in exchange for higher liability caps (tradeoff).
- Can accept opt-out from training for an annual fee or for a Dedicated deployment.

Scripts & one-liners for Sales/SEs (short):
- When they ask for no cap: "I hear wanting full protection — we can offer a higher cap tied to your spend tier and add specific carve-outs for fraud/gross negligence."
- When they demand source code access: "We don't open-source the runtime; we can provide review under NDA and escrow options for critical continuity scenarios."
- On export/residency: "We can guarantee data never leaves region for Dedicated/Private and for hosted we'll provide contractual and technical controls plus an approved fallback plan for emergencies."

Escalation triggers (when to loop legal/engineering/Security):
- Any clause that creates open-ended financial exposure or cyber-exposure (loop Legal + Finance).
- Requests for infra-level access or source code (loop Eng + Sec).
- Specific vertical compliance asks (HIPAA, GLBA, PCI) — loop Compliance and Solutions Eng.
- Customer insists on training rights that give them IP claim over model weights — loop Applied ML + Legal.

Unresolved hypotheses (testing during next 3 deals):
- Hypothesis A: Sales will accept escrow-lite + higher fee for training opt-out in 60% of deals in finance+healthcare. Test: offer as structured add-on.
- Hypothesis B: Engineering will accept SOC2 + scoped audit in lieu of full infra access in 9/10 cases. Test: collect SE feedback during next 5 audits.
- Hypothesis C: Customers are more likely to drop unlimited liability asks if we give clear SLAs + incident credits. Test: apply in negotiations and measure concession rates.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft standardized training-opt-out addendum (pricing tiers, verification).
- Template language for "emergency cross-region failover" with mandatory notice + encryption + deletion within X hours.
- Run quick poll in #legal-ops on acceptable cap bands by ARR bracket.
- Sync with Applied ML on IP risks when customers claim ownership of model outputs (get examples).

Quick reference snippets (put these in short format for SE one-pager):
- Cap: 12 months fees (higher band for Enterprise, negotiable).
- Audit: SOC2 + scoped on-site with 30 days notice.
- Training: enterprise opt-out; hosted opt-out for fee; Dedicated default opt-out.
- Data return: certified deletion within 45 days; logs retained 90 days.

Final note (meta): keep this doc lean — use as meeting cue cards. Save polished language into contracts repo (github link above) once validated. If something is repeating across deals, push to playbook and add a checkbox in sales checklist so SEs can flag earlier.

-- A.P.
